sections.h2: Where is Oconee County and what does it include?
sections.html:
Oconee County is the westernmost county in South Carolina and borders both Georgia and North Carolina. It measures 673.57 square miles in total, of which 626.56 are land and 47.01 are water, so about 7% of the county sits under lakes.

Walhalla is the county seat and Seneca is the largest community. Westminster is the other town most sellers will recognize, and the lakeside communities of Keowee Key and Chickasaw Point, along with Fair Play and Townville (both partly in Anderson County), also appear on the county's community list.

  • Pickens County lies to the east and Anderson County to the southeast.
  • Jackson, Macon and Transylvania counties in North Carolina border it on the north.
  • Hart, Franklin, Stephens, Habersham and Rabun counties in Georgia sit to the south and west.

A house on a county road near Mountain Rest and a home on Lake Keowee are billed through the same Oconee County offices.

sections.h2: How did Oconee County get its name and shape?
sections.html:
Oconee County was formed in 1868 when the state legislature divided Pickens County. The name comes from the Cherokee word Ae-quo-nee, usually given as "land beside the water."

That description fits the county today. Lake Hartwell, Lake Keowee and Lake Jocassee cover large areas, and the state parks and preserves around them include Devils Fork State Park, Oconee State Park and Stumphouse Mountain Heritage Preserve.

For a seller, lakefront and hillside parcels can raise questions about access and shoreline rules that a town lot does not, so ask the county offices what applies to your address.

sections.h2: What jobs and industries support the Oconee County housing market?
sections.html:
Manufacturing is the largest employment sector in Oconee County, at 24.8% of jobs in the third quarter of 2023, followed by retail trade at 16.0%. County output in 2022 was about $4.5 billion, or roughly $56,008 per person.

Employers named in the county's profile include Apex Tool Group, BorgWarner, Duke Energy, Prisma Health, Sandvik, Schneider Electric and Walmart. The Oconee Nuclear Station is also among the county's listed landmarks.

sections.h2: When are Oconee County property taxes due, and how do you pay them?
sections.html:
Oconee County property taxes (other than vehicles) are due by January 15, after a notice that arrives in the fall. For 2026 the county expected online notices by October 10 and printed notices in the mail by October 20, and it said those dates could change.

State law puts the payable window between September 30 and January 15 (S.C. Code 12-45-70). If the due date falls on a weekend or a county holiday it moves to the next business day, and a mailed payment counts if it is postmarked by the deadline.

  • Cards (Discover, MasterCard, Visa) carry a 2.35% processing charge in the office and online.
  • An online e-check costs $2.00.
  • Delinquent taxes can only be paid with cash, a money order or certified funds. Personal and company checks are refused.

The Auditor's Office is at 415 S. Pine St. in Walhalla, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The county lists 864-638-4162 for paying taxes and 864-638-4158 for tax notices and other questions.

sections.h2: What penalties apply if the bill is not paid in Oconee County?
sections.html:
Under S.C. Code 12-45-180, a 3% penalty is added after January 15, another 7% if the bill is still open before February 2, and another 5% before March 17. After March 17 the treasurer sends an execution to the officer who collects delinquent taxes.

One sentence in that section matters at closing. If title moved during the tax year, the tax notice went to the previous owner, and the new owner never got a timely notice, penalties are waived. The seller should still pass along any notice that arrives after the deed records.

Oconee County runs its own tax sale through the Delinquent Tax Office, which you can reach at 864-638-4147. The county advertises each sale in the Seneca Journal Tribune for three weeks and only pre-registered bidders may bid.

sections.h2: What happens in an Oconee County tax sale, and can the owner get the house back?
sections.html:
A tax sale in Oconee County is an auction of the property to the highest bidder, and the owner has one year from the sale date to redeem. The sale is a collection method under S.C. Code Title 12, Chapter 51.

The owner, a grantee from the owner, or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem by paying the taxes, assessments, penalties and costs plus interest on the full bid. That interest rises by quarter.

  • Months 1 to 3: 3%
  • Months 4 to 6: 6%
  • Months 7 to 9: 9%
  • Final three months: 12%

A winning bidder who fails to pay by 4:00 p.m. on sale day is liable for $500 per parcel. Property nobody bids on goes to the county's Forfeited Land Commission for the amount owed. If the year passes with no redemption, the property is conveyed by quitclaim deed, generally within 30 days.

sections.h2: How do you appeal an Oconee County assessment?
sections.html:
You start with a written objection to the Assessor within 90 days of the date on the assessment notice. If no notice was sent that year, the county says you may object until January 15 of the following year.

  1. Send your name, address and phone, a description of the property, your reasons, your estimate of fair market value and supporting documents.
  2. The Assessor reviews the file, sets a conference, may inspect the property and answers in writing.
  3. Within 30 days of that answer, give written notice to appeal to the Board of Assessment Appeals at 415 S. Pine St., Walhalla.
  4. Within 30 days of the Board's decision, ask the Administrative Law Judge Division in Columbia for a contested case hearing.

If the appeal will probably not be settled by December 31, you must pay 80% of the tax on your proposed assessment, and you can ask in writing for a 100% bill. The result can be no change, a lower value or a higher one, so weigh that risk. The Assessor can be reached at 864-638-4150.

sections.h2: What does the 4% legal residence rate mean when you sell in Oconee County?
sections.html:
The 4% rate applies to the owner's legal residence and up to five contiguous acres, and other real property is assessed at 6% (S.C. Code 12-43-220). Oconee County says the school tax credit on owner-occupied homes is automatic once the 4% ratio is granted.

The home cannot be rented for more than 72 days in a calendar year. If an owner loses eligibility and does not tell the Assessor within six months, the statute allows a penalty of 100% of the tax paid plus interest at 0.5% per month, with a $30 minimum.

A seller who moved out and rented the house for a year should expect the 6% rate to apply, and a cash buyer will price the carrying cost accordingly. To check which rate your parcel has, call the Assessor at 864-638-4150.

sections.h2: What is the cost of transferring a deed in Oconee County?
sections.html:
South Carolina charges a deed recording fee of $1.85 for each $500 of value, made up of $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county (S.C. Code 12-24-10 and 12-24-90). A deed given to a lender in lieu of foreclosure, or a foreclosure deed, is on the exempt list in 12-24-40.

Property valuation is also tied to the sale. Under the five-year appraisal rule in 12-43-217, the county revalues every fifth year, and the Assessor must send a notice when value changes by $1,000 or more. Oconee County's own pages do not state its next reassessment year, so ask the Assessor.

Taxes do not disappear at closing. They are normally prorated between the parties, and any bill open in January should be paid from the proceeds so a new owner never inherits a penalty.

sections.h2: What do Oconee County sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
Sellers in Oconee County most often face an inherited house with years of unpaid tax, a lake or hillside property that needs repairs before a bank will lend, or a rental that has turned into a burden. Each has a tax angle.

  • Heirs selling a family house should ask the Assessor whether the 4% rate is still attached.
  • An owner who is behind should call the Delinquent Tax Office at 864-638-4147 before the sale is advertised.
  • A cash buyer does not depend on a lender's appraisal to close.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses as they stand, so a seller does not need to make repairs before asking for an offer. Check the tax figure with the county office first, and we can work from it.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Oconee County SC?
faqs.a: By January 15, with notices going out in the fall. The county expected online notices by October 10 and mailed notices by October 20 for 2026.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Oconee County taxes late?
faqs.a: A 3% penalty applies after January 15, then another 7% before February 2 and another 5% before March 17. After March 17 the bill goes to collection.

faqs.q: How long do you have to appeal an Oconee County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the date on the assessment notice to object in writing to the Assessor. If no notice was issued, the county allows an appeal until January 15 of the following year.

faqs.q: Can I redeem my house after an Oconee County tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes, for one year from the sale date, by paying the taxes, costs and penalties plus interest of 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% depending on the quarter. After that the property is conveyed to the buyer.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Oconee County property taxes?
faqs.a: Call 864-638-4162 to pay, 864-638-4158 for tax notices, the Assessor at 864-638-4150 for values, or Delinquent Tax at 864-638-4147. All offices are at 415 S. Pine St., Walhalla.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Oconee County house if taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. Back taxes are paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and Cash Home Buyers can buy the house as it is and work out the payoff with the county.
